title: Predicted signaling pathways involved in the pathogenesis of meningiomas and EGFL6 as a potential novel serum biomarker for benign meningiomas

publications.title: Analysis of gene expression profiling in meningioma: deregulated signaling pathways associated with meningioma and EGFL6 overexpression in benign meningioma tissue and serum.

institution: Department of Endocrinology, Huashan Hospital, Shanghai Medical College, Fudan University
platform: Affymetrix GeneChip Human Genome U133 Plus 2.0 Array (GPL570)
processed_data_format: GSE32197_series_matrix.txt.gz (normalized expression values) plus raw Affymetrix CEL files in GSE32197_RAW.tar
needs_manual_review_reason: DEEP-AUDIT CORRECTION (2026-07-14): corresponding_author corrected from 'Xuanchun Wang' to 'Ye Gong, Ying Mao'. Wang X is the FIRST author (never marked corresponding); verified directly against the paper's own PLoS One XML markup (PMC3532066): <contrib-group> shows the <xref ref-type="corresp" rid="cor1"> marker attached only to Gong Y and Mao Y (not Wang X), and the <author-notes><corresp id="cor1"> footnote reads '* E-mail: yyeegong@yahoo.com.cn (YG); yingmao168@hotmail.com (YM)' -- i.e. Ye Gong and Ying Mao are the paper's two designated corresponding authors. The prior value had assumed the record's namesake/first author was corresponding, exactly the author-list-position error this audit was asked to catch. Authors array (13 names) already matches PubMed/Europe PMC's full authorString exactly; no truncation found. EXTREMELY SMALL COHORT, flagged deliberately rather than silently extracted at face value. Never previously fetched; identified only as a plausible candidate in this project's first search session (2026-07-10) and independently verified fresh this session via the live BioStudies API (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/api/v1/studies/E-GEOD-32197), which mirrors GEO series GSE32197, cross-checked against GEO's own acc.cgi record. Confirmed genuinely new (grepped GSE32197 across all of /data/, zero hits) and genuinely in-scope (real human patient meningioma tissue, not a cell line), but the array-based expression profiling arm of this study is far smaller than the paper's overall cohort: only 3 GSM records are deposited under this accession (GSM797806 'brain arachnoidal tissue', GSM797807 'fibroblastic meningioma', GSM797808 'anaplastic meningioma'), confirmed directly by GEO per-sample title/source-name/characteristics text. This matches the linked publication's (Wang et al., PLoS One 2012, PMID 23285163) own abstract, which describes the Affymetrix microarray step as the initial pathway-discovery screen ('we established differential gene expression profiles between meningiomas and brain arachnoidal tissue by using Affymetrix GeneChip Human U133 Plus 2.0 Array'), with the paper's much larger validation cohorts (qRT-PCR on additional tissue samples, serum ELISA across many patients and other tumor types) carried out by non-array methods not deposited under this or any other accession. grade_breakdown maps the single fibroblastic sample to WHO grade I (benign) and the single anaplastic sample to WHO grade III, per standard WHO terminology for these histological descriptors (not independently re-stated as a numeric grade anywhere in the deposited metadata itself, so should be re-checked against the paper's own grade table before this record is used in any grade-stratified analysis). Precedent for extracting a core record with an n this small already exists in this inventory (e.g. gse-234402-scrnaseq, sample_count=1). tags.large_cohort left false pending centralized quartile recomputation.
